1.why: All MFA endpoints resolve the account solely from the server-side session via owner()/pendingOwner(), never from a client-supplied user identifier, so settings always belong to the signed-in user.

2.why: Identity codes are bound to the session's emailHash entry in identityLimits and TOTP/backup codes are hashed per account, so a code issued for one account cannot verify another.

3.why: /api/mfa/confirm only clears o.s.enrollment and sets a.mfa=true; it never iterates the global sessions map, so any other pre-existing session for that user remains valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext (enc/dec with a random key) and backup codes as PBKDF2-SHA256 (210k iterations, salt+pepper) hashes.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, backup codes and identity codes all use node:crypto randomBytes/randomInt.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and nothing is written to localStorage/sessionStorage; secrets and CSRF tokens live only in transient JS variables (though also echoed to console).

7.why: Server validates email with a regex and length cap, enforces strict /^\d{6}$/ and backup-code format regexes, rejects non-object or oversized JSON bodies, and uses no SQL at all (in-memory Maps).

8.why: The client renders exclusively via document.createElement with textContent/setAttribute and no innerHTML, and a nonce-based CSP forbids inline scripts.

9.why: The application issues no redirects whatsoever (only JSON responses and one HTML page), so no open-redirect path exists, albeit no explicit allow-list is implemented.

10.why: Every response sets HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control: no-store and a nonce CSP with frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: sessionCookie() and clearCookie() both emit HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict with Path=/ and Max-Age.

12.why: Although stack traces are suppressed (generic 500 message) and nothing is placed in URLs, the server returns mockCode/mockOtp/secret/backup codes in responses and the client explicitly console.logs the identity code, authenticator OTP and all recovery codes.

13.why: Identity codes have a 10-minute expiry plus a used flag, TOTP steps are recorded in usedTotp/e.used to block replay, and backup codes carry used flags and expiry timestamps.

14.why: recordFailure locks after 5 failures for 10 minutes on identity, source-IP, enrollment and account counters, with an additional 30-second request cooldown returning 429.

15.why: The old session is deleted and a fresh id/CSRF issued after identity verification and again after MFA verification; getSession enforces 30-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
